contract_name: Canonical JSON and digest profile (rfc8785-jcs vs legacy sort_keys/ensure_ascii)

registry_v1_3_mapping: r08-v1 digests ('sha256:'+hex, record_digest over record without record_digest, payload_digest) use the legacy S03 form; no canonical_profile member exists in r08-v1 records (docs/r08-s01-contract.md section 2). Registry commit ce00520f91bf3986a08b4d13a1fb062057babc71
required_action: Declare r08-v1 canonicalization as the named legacy profile (ADR-P01 explicitly permits a named historical profile) and bind it to contract_version; any consumer that must verify both needs both implementations. Alternative, cheaper before any pin is approved: define the next record contract (r08-v2) on rfc8785-jcs. Either is an ADR-level technical decision, not an operator one.
notes: Observable difference: ensure_ascii escapes non-ASCII to \uXXXX while JCS emits raw UTF-8; key order differs for supplementary-plane keys (UTF-16 code unit vs code point order). Digests of identical logical content therefore differ for non-ASCII payloads; ASCII-only, integer-only content is byte-identical except key-order edge cases. r08-v1 identifiers are restricted, but payload entries only exclude control/separator/'*' characters, so non-ASCII is representable. ADR-P01 predates r08-v1 (2026-10-22 vs 2026-10-24) and r08-v1 does not cite it. Candidate C2 (borderline, resolvable by naming).
